name: Airtable
verdict: Self-serve: register an OAuth integration at airtable.com/create/oauth, with no app review but public Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs required before others can authorize. Enterprise admins can block or allow-list integrations.
needGuide: Short one: publish your ToS and privacy pages, register the integration, ship.

auth.detail: Authorization code grant with PKCE (S256 only; docs list code_challenge/verifier as non-optional, so treat as required). Access token 60 min; refresh token 60 days, rotating (each refresh invalidates the previous pair). Client secret is optional (use one for server-side exchange). Auth at airtable.com/oauth2/v1/authorize, token at airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token. Redirect URIs must be exact-match HTTPS (HTTP only for localhost).

approval.gate: No app review documented. Before anyone other than the developer can authorize, the integration must have a Terms of Service URL and Privacy Policy URL (support email optional). Enterprise customers' admins can block users from authorizing OAuth integrations, or allow-list specific integrations by Client ID.

scopes.why: Granular scopes plus per-base selection by the user; no scope triggers review.
scopes.summary: Granular scopes set on the integration (records read/write, schema read/write, webhooks, comments, user email). Tokens reach only granted scopes and only the bases the user selected. Exact scope names not re-verified this session (see Scopes reference). No scope documented as triggering review.

prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Airtable user can register an integration; it is tied to the creating account, so create it from a company-owned account rather than a personal one (likely; ownership transfer not documented).

Where you register: airtable.com/create/oauth → Register new OAuth integration → enter name + redirect URL → Register integration → add scopes, then fill Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL, Support email

registerAt.path: airtable.com/create/oauth → Register new OAuth integration → enter name + redirect URL → Register integration → add scopes, then fill Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL, Support email

steps.do: Publish public Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and a support email address for the product
Go to airtable.com/create/oauth and click Register new OAuth integration with a unique name and your HTTPS callback URL
Select minimum scopes (e.g. data.records:read/write, schema.bases:read) and generate a client secret; store it in a secrets manager
Implement authorization code + PKCE (S256), exchange the code within 10 minutes, and store the rotating refresh token atomically
Fill ToS, Privacy Policy and support email on the integration page so outside users can authorize
Test with a second Airtable account on a different workspace; verify refresh, revoke, and base-selection behavior
Give Enterprise customers your Client ID so their admin can allow-list it

roles.team: Any Airtable user can register an integration; it is tied to the creating account, so create it from a company-owned account rather than a personal one (likely; ownership transfer not documented).
roles.customer: The end user authorizes and picks which workspaces/bases to grant; they cannot grant more than they hold. On Enterprise, an admin may block base/workspace selection, block OAuth authorization entirely, or allow only listed Client IDs, so customer IT may need to allow-list your Client ID.

testing: Authorize with your own account against your own bases immediately; the consent dialog can be previewed once at least one scope is added.
The ToS/privacy URL requirement applies to non-development use.

blockers.problem: Others cannot authorize until ToS and Privacy Policy URLs are set
blockers.fix: Add them before the first external pilot.

blockers.problem: Refresh tokens rotate and die after 60 days unused
blockers.fix: Persist the new token on every refresh and serialize refreshes per user (409 means a recent refresh).

blockers.problem: Enterprise admins may block OAuth or require allow-listing by Client ID
blockers.fix: Ship a one-page admin note with your Client ID.

blockers.problem: Redirect mismatch returns no error at all
blockers.fix: Register the exact URI and avoid redirecting from it.

automation.agentCan: Draft ToS/privacy copy, write the PKCE and refresh-rotation code, build the base/workspace picker UX, run test calls, and draft the admin allow-list note.
automation.humanMust: Sign in and register the integration, generate the client secret, approve legal documents, and coordinate Enterprise admin allow-listing.

uncertain: Exact scope names, rate limits, whether integrations support co-owners, and any Airtable Marketplace listing process were not confirmed.
No community sources consulted (search/fetch budgets ran out).
